evidence.note: Ran `go test ./internal/fsm/cli/ ./internal/taskdone/ ./internal/fsm/judge/ -count=1`: all green. `go tool cover -func` reports 100.0% of statements for every function in internal/fsm/cli/run.go.

Mutation-tested each new guard by copying the tree to a scratchpad (rsync, repo untouched), deleting or inverting the line, and running `go test ./...`. Ten mutations survived the full suite; each survivor is reported below with its file:line.

Golden regenerated from TemplateStillPresentCalibration and pinned by TestJ1Goldens (judge_test.go:99-160), which additionally asserts, independently of the golden, that calibration is never fenced and that the product template equals calibration plus the confidence line. No finding.

findings.note: Spec-contract test row unimplemented: `--replace` on `record node-output` is wired but pinned by nothing. spec 5 §7 (docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:296) requires "ERR_NODE_OUTPUT_EXISTS then --replace succeeds". The string "--replace" occurs nowhere in internal/fsm/cli/cli_test.go (0 hits), ERR_NODE_OUTPUT_EXISTS is never asserted in the package, and replacing `Replace: p.bools["replace"]` with `Replace: false` at run.go:638 passes `go test ./...` cleanly. The flag is advertised in AgentPrompt (prompt.go) and in the spec's CLI grammar, so a regression that drops it is invisible.

Spec-contract test row unimplemented: the `fsm export` value oracle. spec 5 §7 (fsm-cli.md:310-312) requires `init --var SECRET=sekret-value` -> default export contains the value in no byte and `manifest.redacted` is non-empty, and `--include-vars --out d` -> present. cli_test.go:286-295 exercises only the default export and the two ERR_EXPORT_DEST refusals; no test ever passes `--include-vars` together with `--out`. Replacing `IncludeVars: p.bools["include-vars"]` with `IncludeVars: false` at run.go:927 passes `go test ./...`. This is the one knob the docs describe as un-redacting run vars ("weakens a guardrail", driving-a-workflow.md:88-92), so its CLI wiring being unpinned is the wrong place for a gap.

Duplicated guard, tested in one copy only: the init-side refusal of a mock scenario outside the repository is unpinned. Deleting run.go:273-275 (`if _, inside := relInside(root, dir); !inside { ... CodeMockInvalid ... "outside" }`) passes `go test ./...`. The two cli_test.go rows that look like they cover it (line 394 `--mock-ai /elsewhere`, line 395 `--mock-ai nodir`) are both satisfied by the fake MockLoad failing on a directory that does not exist, so neither distinguishes "outside the repo" from "missing". The identical guard in the second copy, wiring.go:125-127 (scenarioFor), IS pinned: deleting that one makes the suite fail. A real scenario directory that exists outside the repository is accepted at init today with no test noticing.

A landed fix with no regression test: the ctx-cancellation guard in `judge --run`. run.go:784-786 returns a zero `run.LLMCallData` when `ctx.Err() != nil`, and machine.go:1063 (`if data.Kind == "" { return 0, cerr }`) is what turns that into "append nothing". Without the guard the closure returns `d` with `d.Kind = k` non-empty, so an interrupted call is written into audit.jsonl as a completed `llm_call` with a zero verdict. Deleting the three-line guard passes `go test ./...`. Commit cde8d0a is titled "fix: round-six blockers - cancellation, ..."; the fix is here, the test that would keep it here is not.

shardwiring_test.go asserts a property it does not check, and its sibling file does: the fakeWriter's Write comment (shardwiring_test.go:67-70) states "Write can fail after the pack set is already in place, so it returns a usable rollback alongside the error; the caller must run it" — but TestTaskDonePackWriteFailureFailsTheRun (line 174) never reads `writer.rollbacks`. Deleting `if packRollback != nil { _ = packRollback() }` from internal/taskdone/review.go:165-168 leaves the whole taskdone package green. internal/prready/shardwiring_test.go:180-190 has exactly the missing test (`TestPackWriteErrorRunsRollback`, "rollbacks = %d, want 1: a failed pack write must be rolled back"), so the assertion was written for one of the two identical wirings only.

The new housekeeping test pins the positive direction of the GC gate but not the negative one it exists for. review.go:267-271 comments "Superseded result files are collected only once the gate has passed, so a failing run never destroys the record it was judged on" and guards GC with `if !result.Blocking`. Removing that guard (calling GC unconditionally) passes `go test ./...`. TestTaskDoneHousekeepingFailuresDoNotDiscardTheRun's "gc" case proves GC IS reached when the gate passes (shardwiring_test.go:240-245), and TestTaskDonePackRollbackRunsWhenTheReviewFails' `collections != 0` check (line 206) is on the early-return error path, before the housekeeping block, so it never reaches the guard. The fix is one line: the same table's "prune" case is already a blocking run, so asserting `tc.writer.collections == 0` there would pin it.

Dead code that reads as an alias mapping which does not exist. `judge.KindStillPresent` is the literal "still-present" (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:19), so both `if k == "still-present" { k = judge.KindStillPresent }` blocks in `judge()` — run.go:713-715 and again at run.go:744-746 after judgeInput — are no-ops. Deleting either (verified independently) passes `go test ./...`. The duplication in particular suggests someone believed the wire name and the constant differed.

`--judge-model`/`--judge-effort` and METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL/METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT are accepted on the fork path and silently discarded. parseArgs (run.go:113) accepts them for every subcommand; `init()` folds them into the run's vars via applyJudgeOverrideFor (run.go:307), but `fork()` builds `machine.ForkOptions{... Vars: p.vars ...}` at run.go:573 with no override, so `advance --run X --from Y --judge-model m` parses cleanly, exits 0, and the child keeps the parent's judge. Three documents state these "retarget the judge exactly as --var JUDGE does" (prompt.go AgentPrompt, docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md:89-91, skills/fsm/SKILL.md:57-58) — and `--var JUDGE=` genuinely does work on a fork (SKILL.md:47 documents it as the judge-swap recipe), so the two are not equivalent exactly where the docs say they are. Also note `applyJudgeOverride` (wiring.go:254, the 3-arg wrapper) has no production caller at all: only judgeoverride_test.go:45/57/63 invoke it.

A doc comment that talks the reader out of a check the code does not make. run.go:341-342: "events reads a run's log ... (nil when the store cannot read it; the envelope then omits the derived key rather than failing a command that already succeeded)". No caller omits anything. `lastTransitionGate` and `handler` return a nil `any` that marshals to JSON `null` (present, not omitted), and `failedFrom` returning `("", 0)` feeds `resumeHint` at run.go:414 and run.go:502, producing `metareview fsm advance --run <id> --from  --at-iter 0` — a malformed command emitted under the `resume_hint` key that the AgentPrompt instructs the agent to run verbatim on GATE_FAILED. If the intent is genuinely "omit", the keys should be conditional; if the intent is "this cannot happen after a successful Open", the comment should say that instead.

`gate --input` misreports its own SHA validation and the check is unpinned. run.go:677 is `if err := dec.Decode(&snap); err != nil || snap.FixEntryHead != "" && !gate.ValidSHA(snap.FixEntryHead)`, and the branch reports `in.usage("--input is not a snapshot: " + fmt.Sprint(err))`. On the ValidSHA half `err` is nil, so the operator is told `--input is not a snapshot: <nil>` with no mention of the malformed fix_entry_head that actually caused it. Deleting the `|| snap.FixEntryHead != "" && !gate.ValidSHA(...)` clause passes `go test ./...`; `fix_entry_head` appears nowhere in cli_test.go.

Doc-comment attached to the wrong declaration: run.go:182 "// openRun resolves --run, peeks the init line for the mock scenario, builds the wiring, and opens the run." sits immediately above `type opened struct` (run.go:183), not above `func (in *invocation) openRun` (run.go:191). godoc renders openRun's description as the documentation for the `opened` type, and openRun itself is undocumented.

Error-code remapping by prose match. `converge()` at run.go:869 re-codes ERR_BAD_CONVERGENCE to ERR_CMD_NOT_ALLOWED when the detail `strings.Contains(..., "unknown cmd")`, and `cmdNameIn` (run.go:878-883) recovers the command name by taking the substring after the last space and trimming quotes. The contract is therefore the exact wording of internal/fsm/converge/converge.go:169 (`"line %d: unknown cmd %q"`); rewording that message silently downgrades the CLI's code and corrupts the `name` field, with no test pinning the pair. A typed field on the converge error would remove the coupling.

TestTaskDonePackRollbackRunsWhenTheReviewFails (shardwiring_test.go:186-211) makes itself pass by construction when the environment defeats its setup: it chmods the review directory to 0555 and calls `t.Skip("the review body unexpectedly succeeded; nothing proved")` if Create returns nil. Under any uid for which 0555 is not a write barrier (root, some CI containers, some filesystems) the test silently proves nothing while still reporting a non-failure. A skip is more honest than a green pass, but the rollback invariant then has no coverage at all in this package — see the medium finding above, which it shares a cause with.
